scope: Offline controlled TGN mechanism experiment on existing deidentified numerical matrices; no attack generation or replay
design: Full factorial 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, separately on two datasets, three fixed initialization seeds. 96 actual fits.

factors.current: 1 original readout, 0 zero vector only at current-feature readout; endpoints and historical messages remain available
factors.history: 1 original TGN observation/memory, 0 never observe messages; learned endpoint embeddings remain
factors.drop: 0 original negative loss, 1 exclude negative examples with exactly unchanged endpoint pair; keep normal-class loss

fixed: Original protocol: full train/calibration/test, 12 epochs, 512 batch, seeds 11 29 47, 2 CPU threads. Each cell trained from scratch; no inference-only distribution-shift ablation.
outcomes: AP and recall/FPR at calibration-only 0.1% and 1%; paired factor differences at identical dataset/seed/other conditions; no test-optimized thresholds, sign flips or best-seed selection
mechanism_questions: Does any gain survive removal of current request readout?
Does any gain survive removal of dynamic history while retaining endpoint embeddings?
Does context help specifically when history/current path is enabled?
Do exact-pair negative collisions change the observed effects?
limits: Mechanistic interventions concern this implementation and these fixed datasets, not independent deployments or the cause of actual malicious impact
Current-off and history-off do not remove endpoint identity embeddings
Dropping exact-pair collisions does not remove all globally benign negative edges or inconsistent historical attributes
Context changes input width and parameter count
Published Granomaly differs in additional architecture details: these interventions cannot uniquely attribute its entire gap
Already inspected datasets: retrospective analysis; no universal superiority claim
